original_question: Let H be Green’s H-relation on a semigroup, let ∼tr be the epigroup conjugacy relation, and let ∼p∗ be the transitive closure of the relation a ∼p b defined by factorizations a = uv and b = vu. Must every pair of H-related elements that are ∼tr-conjugate also be ∼p∗-conjugate, that is, is ∼tr ∩ H contained in ∼p∗ for all semigroups?

refined_question: Let S be an epigroup. Define Green’s H-relation on S by a H b iff aS^1 = bS^1 and S^1a = S^1b. Define primary conjugacy by a∼p b iff a=uv and b=vu for some u,v∈S, and let ∼p∗ be the transitive closure of ∼p. Define epigroup conjugacy by a∼tr b iff there exist g,h∈S^1 such that ghg=g, hgh=h, hg=a^ω, gh=b^ω, and ga^{ω+1}h=b^{ω+1}. Is it always true that a H b and a∼tr b imply a∼p∗ b; equivalently, does ∼tr ∩ H ⊆ ∼p∗ hold for every epigroup S? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft because it matches the exact open sentence after Theorem 4.1 while restoring the hidden epigroup hypothesis from Section 2. The Section 4 setup introduces H and the inclusion chain ∼p∗ ∩ H ⊆ ∼tr ∩ H, so the intended scope is precisely the reverse-inclusion question for H-related trace-conjugate pairs. One caution: the surrounding text appears internally inconsistent, since Theorem 4.1 and the immediately following SmallSemigroup(5,255) paragraph present ∼p∗ ∩ H as a proper subset of ∼tr ∩ H, which would already negate the literal open question; nevertheless, your draft is clearly aimed at that explicit open-problem sentence rather than a broader neighboring problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
